The printer's exterior body is predominantly white plastic.
Front and upper panels appear to be clear transparent material (likely acrylic or polycarbonate) allowing an unobstructed view of the interior.
Interior guide rods and some structural rails are metallic (silver/steel appearance).
The build plate appears dark on its surface and rests on a glass-looking substrate with a greenish tinge at the front edge.
spatial: The transparent front panel forms the main viewing window; the build plate lies horizontally near the bottom of the interior directly behind this front window.
The printer carriage with the 'Ultimaker' label is mounted on a horizontal rail spanning the upper interior and sits above the build plate.
Two vertical metal rods are positioned toward the rear of the interior, behind the carriage, running from the base toward the top of the enclosure.
A tall cylindrical/box-shaped white component is located at the right-rear interior, behind the carriage and near the right interior wall.
A clear/transparent top panel is attached above the main body, forming an upper enclosure that sits above the visible interior components.
uncertainties: Small text, iconography and labels on the lower front panel (near the display and control knob) are not legible at this image resolution and are transcribed here as [unreadable] if needed; the display itself is blank or too low-contrast to read.
The precise wording/format of the printer model marking (for example superscript formatting) is interpreted as 'Ultimaker 3' but exact glyph details may differ.
Some interior parts (for example whether the cylindrical rear unit is a filament spool holder or another component) cannot be identified confidently from appearance alone.
Fasteners, small stickers and any fine-print safety or certification labels are present but unreadable in this image.

Because only a single viewpoint is provided, counts reflect only individually distinguishable visible objects and do not imply total room inventory or the presence of other equipment outside the frame.

baseline_candidates.text:
Title: Digital Learning Studio
Section: Text and spatial information: workstation close-up
Image-derived evidence:
The Digital Learning Studio close-up shows the back of a monitor labeled "DELL", supported by a silver pedestal. To its left stands a black tower labeled "Antec" with a transparent side panel, a visible internal fan and metal securing brackets. A small "CAUTION" label is visible, but its fine print is unreadable. A foreground keyboard bears the label "LEGION". Cables and keyboards lie on the desk, and additional workstations with red and blue chairs appear behind it. These labels do not identify the processor, graphics card or complete computer model.

Title: Multi-Purpose Room
Section: Spatial information
Image-derived evidence:
The Multi-Purpose Room plaque is a horizontal rectangular sign with a dark frame, mounted on a white wall. Its upper black band carries the room identifier in white, and its lower light-brown wood-grain panel carries the room name in black. The image shows the plaque rather than the room interior, so equipment, seating capacity and interior layout cannot be determined.

Title: Wet Lab - Culture Room
Section: Spatial information
Image-derived evidence:
The Wet Lab - Culture Room plaque is a horizontal rectangular sign with a dark frame, mounted on a white wall. Its upper black band carries the room identifier in white, and its lower light-brown wood-grain panel carries the room name in black. The image shows the plaque rather than the room interior, so equipment, seating capacity and interior layout cannot be determined. The nested source folder records the supplied grouping under Thematic Workshop G; the plaque alone does not establish an internal doorway or passage between the rooms.

title: Row of bench machines and workstations with LaserPro signage
facts: No people are visible in the photographed scene.

At least five large freestanding equipment cabinets/machines are visible in a single row along the wall (from right edge toward left): a blue-and-white GCC-branded machine at the right foreground, a white tall cabinet immediately to its left, a blue GCC machine with a clear lid/cover further left, a white tall unit left of that, and a beige/tan tall unit at the far left. These five distinct housings are individually visible; overlap and partial cropping prevent confirming if additional similar units extend beyond the image edges.
Two desktop computer monitors are visible on the bench between the blue GCC machine (center-left) and the white tall cabinet (center-right).
Two desktop keyboards and two mice are visible on the bench below the two monitors.
Two swivel chairs (light grey plastic seats with black five-star caster bases) are positioned at the bench in front of the two monitors.
Three vertically routed flexible exhaust/vent ducts (grey ribbed hoses) run from near the machines up toward the ceiling, visible behind the row of equipment.
Three wall-mounted grey electrical/connector boxes are visible on the wall above the bench to the right of the monitors.
Multiple small printed labels and stickers appear on machine panels and lids, but most are partially obscured or too small to read in detail.
The floor is a pale mint/very light green smooth surface (likely vinyl or painted concrete).
Several machines have blue panels (medium blue) combined with white or light-grey housings; the GCC-branded machines are predominantly blue and white.
The tall cabinets to the left are beige/tan and white respectively, with smooth painted metal surfaces.
The bench surface appears white and the two chairs are light grey plastic seats with black metal/plastic caster bases.
The flexible exhaust ducts are grey and ribbed, suggesting a plastic or corrugated material.
spatial: The equipment and cabinets form a linear row placed against the right-side wall, extending from the right foreground toward the left background.
A bench workspace with two monitors, two keyboards and two mice sits between the two central machines: the blue GCC machine (center-left) and the white tall cabinet (center-right).
Two light-grey swivel chairs are positioned in front of the bench, one in front of each monitor and keyboard pair.

Three flexible grey ducts rise from the area behind the machines and run upward toward the ceiling; they are spaced roughly along the row of equipment and appear attached behind or near individual machines.

Three grey wall-mounted boxes are located on the wall immediately above the bench to the right of the monitors; a printed sign reading 'LaserPro Spirit Main Power' is mounted near those boxes with downward-pointing arrows.
uncertainties: Exact model names and small label text on the machine panels and lids are mostly unreadable at this resolution; only the larger readable text has been transcribed.
The leftmost beige/tan and adjacent white tall units are partially obscured and cropped by the image edge, so their full counts and identities beyond the visible housings cannot be confirmed.
Some small stickers and labels visible on machine lids and panels are too small or angled to transcribe; their contents are therefore not included.
The precise function or type of each visible machine (e.g., exact equipment categories) cannot be determined from appearance alone and has not been inferred.

The reading 'SpiritLS' and the GCC logos are reasonably legible, but adjacent smaller characters or numbers that might form full model identifiers are not readable; those possible fragments were not completed.

baseline_candidates.text:
Title: Makerspace A
Section: Spatial information: shared work tables
Image-derived evidence:
IMG_2679 shows Makerspace A with rows of light-wood-topped tables on pale metal frames, many tall stools with round seats and dark metal legs, and work materials or bags on some surfaces. Large windows run along the left side, with plants visible outside. Exposed ceiling ducts and services sit above numerous rectangular light panels. White cabinets and additional equipment occupy the rear perimeter, and the floor is smooth and light gray. The image does not establish an official capacity or a complete stool, table or equipment count.

Title: Thematic Workshop C
Section: Spatial information: printers and work surfaces
Image-derived evidence:
IMG_2694 and IMG_2695 show overlapping Thematic Workshop C interiors with a pale mint-colored floor, gray wall panels and a large illuminated ceiling. A sink with a tap is on the left work surface. Along the walls are shelves, containers, several enclosed desktop machines, a monitor and computer equipment, with tall stools at the benches. A large black enclosed machine stands near the back beside other devices. The visual views do not identify every model or provide a complete printer count.

Title: Machine Workshop
Section: Spatial information: workshop interiors and material storage
Image-derived evidence:
IMG_2701 and IMG_2702 show Machine Workshop with multiple wooden workbenches, black rolling drawer cabinets, bench-mounted tools and machines, shelves, storage tubs and visible windows around the far side. Long linear lights hang beneath exposed ducts and ceiling services. A light-gray floor runs between the benches, and gray chairs appear near the foreground. The views show the same room from overlapping positions and do not establish a complete machine inventory.

title: 3D printing web form showing Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One selection
facts: Visible location text: Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One
No people are visible in the photographed scene.

User interface elements visible on a mobile device screen include: at least three dropdown boxes (visible labels: "Choose 3D Slicer:", "Choose 3D Printer:", and the location dropdown showing "Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One"), one horizontal progress bar (green) labelled by nearby text "Slice completed.", and one large green rectangular button labelled "Submit Job."

Additional UI sections visible: a heading "Preferences", a subheading/list item area labelled "Available Locations:", a field labelled "Material:" with value "PLA", and a section heading "Slice Settings" containing two collapsed rows labelled "Machine Settings" and "Resolution."

Status indicators from the phone UI are visible at the top of the image: the time "6:38", a location/arrow icon to the right of the time, cellular signal bars, Wi‑Fi icon, and a battery indicator showing "82" inside a green battery icon.
Background of the app content area is white with light grey boxed containers for controls.
The progress bar is solid green and full-width beneath the text "Slice completed."
The "Submit Job" button is a dark green rounded rectangle with white text.
Text is primarily dark grey or black; the dropdown fields and boxes have light grey borders.
spatial: The phone status bar is at the very top of the image showing the time "6:38" on the left and signal/Wi‑Fi/battery indicators on the right.
Below the status bar, a partial area shows a file chooser row with the label "Choose File" and the filename "SDBenchy.stl" partly visible to its right.

Under that, a boxed control labelled "Choose 3D Slicer:" contains the value "Ultimaker CuraEngine" followed by the text "Slice completed." and a full-width green horizontal progress bar directly underneath that caption.
A separate boxed panel titled "Preferences" appears below the slicer area; inside it the left-aligned label "Choose 3D Printer:" is followed by a dropdown field showing "Ultimaker 3 Extended."

Within the same Preferences box the label "Available Locations:" appears above a dropdown showing "Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One", and further down the label "Material:" appears above a field with value "PLA."
Below Preferences, a section titled "Slice Settings" contains two stacked collapsed rows or buttons: the top row reads "Machine Settings" and the lower row reads "Resolution."
At the bottom of the visible screen area, a large green rectangular button labelled "Submit Job" spans nearly the full width of the content area.
ocr: Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One
uncertainties: The top file chooser row shows a filename that appears to be "SDBenchy.stl" but part of that area is slightly cropped and the exact capitalization is taken from visible pixels.
Small icons in the phone status bar (cellular, Wi‑Fi) are visible but their exact signal values other than the battery number "82" are not fully legible.
Any additional small labels or helper text within dropdown fields (such as downward arrows or truncated helper text) are not legible and therefore not transcribed.

No physical room signage, hardware nameplates, or real-world equipment are visible; all counted 'objects' are elements of the mobile app UI. If the request expected identification of physical machines or signage in a room, that information is unknown from the image.

baseline_candidates.text:
Title: Thematic Workshop C
Section: Text information: SLA printing poster and safety card
Image-derived evidence:
The Thematic Workshop C poster in IMG_2692 is titled "SLA 3D PRINTING". It explains that stereolithography cures photopolymer resin layer by layer with UV light to form a three-dimensional object, and lists fast speed, high resolution and smooth surface finishes as advantages. Its guidance panel names "Form 4 SLA 3D printers" and says they are available under tutor guidance, with help in material selection and machine use to create prototypes for learning purposes. This wording does not specify a printer count. A "Creations Gallery" shows three printed examples, including a dragon-like figure, a dental model and a light-colored fabricated piece.

Title: Open Event Area
Section: Spatial information: projector and exit doors
Image-derived evidence:
IMG_2634 shows an Open Event Area projector suspended on an extended scissor-style ceiling mount among angled rectangular light panels and exposed ducts. The image does not establish its model or projection settings. IMG_2636 shows glass double doors with horizontal frosted bands, vertical "PUSH" labels and an illuminated "EXIT" sign with Chinese exit text above them. The Open Event Area blue notice panel and wall controls are immediately to the right.

Title: Brainstorm Space / Brainstorming Area
Section: Text and spatial information: display, lectern and bell
Image-derived evidence:
IMG_2644 shows a large display near Brainstorming Area with a blue circuit-style desktop background, a white freestanding lectern and a dark banner reading "Innovation Academy" and "Faculty of Engineering, HKU". An overhead exit indicator points right in the image. The lectern bears Innovation Wing branding. Screen icons and small banner text are not reliably transcribed.

title: Electronics bench with benchtop instruments and soldering station
facts: No people are visible in the photographed scene.
A single workbench with two long horizontal shelves and a lower work surface occupies the centre of the image.
Four benchtop instruments are visible on the upper shelf; they appear as distinct stacked/side-by-side units (visible count = 4).

One soldering station assembly is visible on the work surface at left-center consisting of a blue and yellow controller unit, a soldering iron in a blue holder, and a small roll of tape adjacent to the holder (visible count = 1 assembly; tape count = 1).
One chair is visible at the right-front of the workbench (visible count = 1).
A set of wall-mounted electrical outlets/sockets is visible on the wall behind the bench (visible count = 2 recessed outlet plates visible).
A cluster of multiple safety/warning labels/stickers is affixed to the top of the left upright frame of the bench (visible count = at least 6 distinct labels/stickers).
One small rectangular sign or label is affixed to the tall white panel at the right edge of the image (visible count = 1).
The workbench surfaces and shelves are a pale, light-coloured wood (plywood edges visible) with a smooth finish.
The bench frame and vertical supports appear light grey, likely painted metal.
The soldering station controller and holder are blue and yellow (blue bodies with yellow control faces/accents).
The benchtop instruments are predominantly light grey or off-white, typical plastic or metal instrument enclosures.
The chair visible at the front right is a muted pale green/grey plastic seat with a smooth matte finish.
Safety/warning labels have high-contrast colours: yellow background for 'Caution' style labels and red/black elements for 'Danger' style labels.
spatial: The two horizontal shelves are integrated into the workbench: one upper shelf holding the four benchtop instruments and a lower raised shelf above the main tabletop that runs the bench length.
The soldering station assembly sits on the main work surface near the left third of the bench, in front of the lower raised shelf and below the upper shelf with instruments.
The wall-mounted electrical outlet plates are located on the wall directly behind and slightly above the lowered shelf, roughly centered horizontally behind the bench.
The chair is positioned in front of the right end of the main work surface, partially tucked under the bench.
The cluster of safety/warning labels is attached to the top of the left vertical support of the bench frame.
A small rectangular sign or label is attached to a tall white panel at the far right edge of the image, separate from the bench structure.
uncertainties: The exact wording of some small labels and stickers in the safety cluster is partially obscured or too small to read; several labels were transcribed from visible fragments and layout but may be incomplete.
The instrument front-panel legends and brand/model identifiers are not fully legible except for the visible label 'M400012'; other instrument text could not be reliably transcribed from the image.
The small rectangular sign on the tall white panel at the right edge contains text that is not legible at this resolution.

The identification of the blue/yellow device as a 'soldering station assembly' is based on visible form (controller, iron, holder) but not on any readable model or function label; the equipment type is described as observed appearance rather than confirmed specification.

title: Workbench with metal mold, hammer and shoe on stained floor
facts: One hammer positioned near the top edge of the image, head visible and lying on the floor.
One clamping assembly / vise attached to the top-right of a rectangular mold-like assembly; the clamp appears to have a screw handle and is partially covered in material.
One rectangular mold-like assembly centrally placed, containing a 3 by 4 grid of filled cells (12 visible cells) with a blue-green substance in each cell.

One shoe and part of a foot (black and white athletic shoe) is visible at the lower-right corner and is cropped by the image edge (count = 1, cropped).
Multiple small loose fragments or chips of the blue-green material are scattered around the mold on the floor (count cannot be exactly determined from the image).
Several metal parts and fixtures are present on and around the mold (individual components visible but not all individually distinguishable for an exact count).
The floor is a beige or tan stained hard surface (likely concrete) with visible scratches and darker scuff marks.
The central grid cells contain a blue-green (teal) substance with lighter, whitish residue or drips along some cell edges.

pages.text:
Performance of Sustainable Cement for Marine Construction
Course project, CIVL4102 Final year project (Coordinator: Dr. Sergio Lourenco)
Project supervisor: Dr. Hailong Ye (Department of Civil Engineering)
Project information
Project descriptions
Chloride attack of concrete in particular for marine structures is a serious global issue where it can lead to severe deterioration of the concrete, drastic reduction in strength of structures and safety concerns. The world is urging for a remedy to this situation. A green alternative to Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC), Alkaline-activated Slag (AAS), is found to be having 70%-150% higher chloride binding capacity than that of OPC, making it a potential antidote to this issue. This project aimed to analyse the chloride resistance of AAS in the marine environment, to provide better predict the service life of marine structures and to find ways to enhance the durability of concrete in aggressive conditions. With AAS, let us ‘cement’ a sustainable future.

The 4th Engineering Inno Show
"All the flowers of all the tomorrows are in the seeds of today"
Date:
4th May 2021 (Tuesday)
Time:
10:00 am – 15:00 pm
(Award ceremony at 12:45pm)
Venue:
Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing
Show me the projects
Event photo gallery
Awards & Prizes
Inno Show Award:
To encourage students to develop innovative mindset in tackling engineering and social problems, and to support outstanding ideas to join international design competitions, the Dean’s Innovation and Entrepreneurship Fund will appropriate an amount of HK$100K
to support a maximum of five student teams
participated in the Inno Show to take part in international design competitions.
A Panel to be chaired by the Associate Dean (Student Development) with the Dean of Engineering as one of the key members, will select the winning teams from the Inno Show event to be held at the end of semester 2, 2020-2021, based on the design put forward by the students, and their presentation during the Inno Show.
About Engineering Inno Show
Previous image
Next image
The Engineering Inno Show is a showcase carnival that celebrates innovative Engineering student projects at the end of every semester. Participating students will have the opportunity to expound on their inventive design, research and projects; harness timely and constructive feedback given by peers, teachers, industry experts and the public through knowledge exchange; and spin talent and ideas into innovative (re)inventions. There are many reasons why Engineering Inno Show is a unique concoction of its missions and vision. We offer a vibrant, inter/multi-disciplinary and hands-on learning platform for students to create their own impact, in and out of the classroom. The showcases also paint junior fellows a concrete picture of what constitutes an exemplary work and open pathways for them to look at Engineering through the lens of their senior cohorts, whether they are from Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Electrical Engineering or Environmental Engineering. We believe that Engineering united with hands-on experience is essential. It is our vision to inspire a generation of intrepid explorers and committed collaborators. At Engineering Inno Show, we are transmitting knowledge and values through narrative. Whether it is communicated in layman’s terms or field-specific terminologies, we hope that the seeds of creative minds will germinate and thrive.

Winners of Inno Show Award
We are excited to announce that the 4th Engineering Inno Show was successfully held on May 4, 2021. A total of 36 student projects from 5 departments and InnoHub members were showcased in the event. The teams have done an excellent job in preparing the event and presenting their work to classmates, teachers, and visitors. Please join us in congratulating the following five projects for receiving the Inno Show Awards:
Introducing SURGIVIEW: A Fast and Accurate Augmented Reality(AR) Application Supporting End-to-End Clinical Operations
SURGIVIEW is a holographic augmented reality (AR) application that can assist end-to-end surgical support for minimally invasive surgeries (MIS). This app can overlay holographic anatomic structure on physical tissue, so surgeons can see “through” patient’s body during operation. Incorporating a novel triplet-calibration algorithm, the app can achieve accurate overlay (re-projection error < 5mm) faster than most of the current strategies for less than 8 seconds.
Aiming for use among medical community including surgeons, patients and medical residents, the app has multiple functions to support from pre-operative planning, intra-operative navigation to post-operative demonstration. With SURGIVIEW, we hope to develop a more intuitive and interactive future of clinical and surgery practices.
ProperT
“The rights of many tenants in Hong Kong are left unenforced. Not only are the relevant regulations and clauses inaccessible and convoluted, it is also hard for the average tenant to know whom to approach when there is a “health and safety” issue in their buildings.
We develop a technology solution that would inform tenants about their rights using computer vision technology. Tenants can simply use their mobile phones to scan items in the common areas of their buildings to learn about the regulations and clauses relevant to those items. This would enable them to anonymously report these breaches for enforcement.”
Impact of Different Factors on Hyporheic Exchange in a Meandering Pool-riffle Stream
The hyporheic zone (HZ) is the region of saturated sediment surrounding a stream which connects surface water and groundwater flow. The overlying water with dissolved matters infiltrates into the HZ, stays there for some time and interacts with groundwater, and exfiltrates out of the HZ, resulting in hyporheic exchanges (HE).
Most of the rivers are designed with narrow bottom section and large upper section of concrete streambed which results in bad river eco-system. In recent decades, more and more stream restoration projects involve the recovery of HE, however, effective guidance in restoring HE is still missing. Therefore, this study aims to examine the effectiveness of different key factors (e.g., stream discharge, slope, sinuosity and groundwater flow) in restoring HZ in a meandering channel with floodplain using flume experiments and numerical simulations.
Design and Modification of a Rototiller for the Grass/Sedge Control
WWF-HK, the management organization of the Mai Po Nature Reserve, has to offer waterbirds a mudflat without vegetation. Currently, workers are deployed into the mudflat to remove the vegetation. However this method is inefficient and dangerous. WWF-HK wishes to develop a product to reduce the necessity of sending out workers to the intertidal mudflat. Field visits were conducted to understand the design constraints. Removal methods adopted by other wetland management in the world were studied. As a result, radio-controlled hovercraft mounted with a grass cutter was chosen as the solution to the problem. The product was tested in different settings, including lawn, water and Mai Po. Results proved the product met the target specification. The product would serve as a reference for WWF-HK in future projects in vegetation removal.
A solar power system for producing useful fuels and chemicals from biomass waste
To design an innovative solar power system with a solar tracking system and solar power supply system, which comprises the concepts of applying solar energy and waste-to-energy, to convert biomass waste materials to char products, namely charcoal, biochar and activated carbon through pyrolysis. The solar power system is a zero-carbon emission system during operation and conversion. Furthermore, it is an economically viable system with a short payback period of less than 7 years with a minimal land requirement. It is hoped that the project will contribute to both environment and lead to the optimization of power storage to discover cost-effective designs in the future.
Projects in the show
Electrical and Electronic Engineering
Drones for the purpose of Long Distance Wireless Communication based on LoRa
The main purpose of this project is to develop a cost-effective surveillance and rescue drone with a longer flying time and long-range data transmission through a careful selection of industrial quality low-cost components. Our target customers are disaster relief teams which can use the drone for assistance in rescue operations through surveillance and human detection.
The drone has the following functionality:
i) Human Detection Capabilities through PIR Sensing
ii) LoRa communication channel for transmitting human detection signals back to rescue teams
iii) Auto-Level Feature to ensure stability in turbulent weather conditions
A first prototype has been developed with all the necessary functionality and is 40% cheaper than available solutions.
Our goals for the next prototype are: i) Reduce weight to improve performance ii) Design a custom PCB to make design more compact.
Read More »
Computer Science
Automatic cars
This project is participating the Robomaster ICRA AI challenge which aims to create an automatic small car which can conduct automatic navigation, decision making, auto-aiming (for shooting other robots). During the competition, robots will automatically navigate in an 8m * 4m competition region with barriers, localize itself, find the enemy robot, aim at its armor, and shoot it!
Read More »
Electrical and Electronic Engineering
Game app for pick and place 3D printed robotic arm
This project proposed to build up a “Compact AlphaGo”. For the software part, an Android chess game application was developed by Flutter with a Flask image processing server which was developed by Python. The Minimax Algorithm and Alpha-Beta Pruning constructed a “brain” to the AI which is embedded inside the Android app. A robotic arm with a chess stacker was built by the 3D modeling software AutoCAD, the cheeses were grasped by the robotic arm precisely and placed on the correct grid of the chessboard.
Read More »
Computer Science
Supermarket Jump!
Supermarket Jump is a minigame where player can take part in a casual parkour experience. The player will play as a box of milk who does not want to be purchased and tried to jump against the conveyer belt to avoid being bought. The main objective of the game is to stay on the conveyer belt as long as possible. The player will encounter various obstacles in the process and some obstacles are deadly – touching them will immediately lead to the end of the game. Bonus points will also be offered if the player successfully performs a “risky jump”.
Read More »
Industrial and Manufacturing Systems Engineering
Logistics delivery trajectories analysis by machine learning
“In traditional logistics operations, activities and their durations were not properly recorded. Thus, it is difficult to understand and model the daily operations.
In this project, with given trajectories, a methodology is proposed to infer the types of activities of the delivery workers in a journey.
The method is to analyze the trajectories which can be identified from the collections of GPS data collected by the devices the deliver worker carried when they are on duty.
We would want to know whether the delivery worker is traveling or delivering the goods given a trajectory segment.”
Read More »
Electrical and Electronic Engineering
Drawing Robot and Selfie Smart Phone App
For the current drawing robot products, the users use the various apps to do the image processing and Bluetooth transmission, the operation is inconvenient and complicated. For improving user experience, there is a mobile app called “Drawing Robot Controller” is developed. Users can use the mobile app to achieve a basic moving control function and image drawing function via clicking the buttons on the app. Unlike the “Printer”, the drawing robot should be “Painter” after integrating with the mobile app. The robot can draw what the user wants in different places with different styles via this app.
Read More »
First Year Engineering
Dance with idols
Dance with idols is a music game. With only one smart phone or PC with one webcam, you can follow the tutorial and dance with virtual idols. The camera captures your gesture and the computer calculates the similarity between you and the model precisely. At the end of each song, you will see your final total score and grade. It lowers the requirement of devices but improves the dancing experience along with virtual idols.
Read More »
Electrical and Electronic Engineering
Augmented Reality in Teaching and Learning
A common difficulty for beginner programmers is the concept of objects and references, which is more apparent when learning Python, which hides these concepts with simple semantics. This project is a mobile application that aims to use AR visualization to teach this concept, using some data types in Python. The user is able to execute supported Python statements and view an AR animation visualizing the components involved and the underlying operation. Their behavior are shown using their AR models and animations. Sandbox mode and exercise mode are available for user to explore on their own or follow exercises that showcase the properties of the data types. With the help of this application, the user can understand the concept of object and reference more clearly.
Read More »
Computer Science
A Big Data Driven Approach for MTR and Corona Virus Analysis
This is a Big-Data project catering to the needs of researchers at The University of Hong Kong. This project’s implementation in the form of a web-based system that enables easy flow of data-retrieval, visualization, and analysis that would fuel research into the fields of COVID-19 spread and MTR passenger behavior.
Read More »
First Year Engineering
Smart Soccer Robot (ii) @ 4th Inno Show
This is a remote-controlled robot designed to play soccer matches against other robots. It is a product aimed at teenagers learning STEM education. Our design is inspired by the shape of a charging bull, which makes it more attractive to our target audience. The robot is made from mBot parts, laser-cut wooden panels, and 3D printed wheels. It is assembled using only a few screws due to our use of interlocking mechanisms integrated into the panels. The robot includes an optical sensor, and displays the number of times it crosses a black line on the seven segment display on the back.
Read More »
Mechanical Engineering
BREED HKU: Robotic Fish@4th Inno Show
The robotic fish project provides aspiring engineers with a platform to gain hands-on experience in applied engineering. With design innovation, we enhance the functionality of the fish to further improve manoeuvrability and control.
Our initial goal to make the robot faster and break the world record again has been achieved. Now, the second goal is to solve real-world problems. From discussions with stakeholders, we have identified an opportunity to apply our robot in data collection for marine exploration and pollution monitoring. It can be used to collect water data such as temperature, pH, etc. and also for real-time mapping and monitoring of specimens in the environment such as coral reefs, microplastics, etc.
We envision a series of such projects under the BREED umbrella to promote bio-robotics with a purpose. Ultimately, we hope to create an organisation that drives social impact through innovative robotics solutions.
Read More »
Electrical and Electronic Engineering
Fire Evacuation Assistance Robot
How occupants can evacuate during emergency in High-Rise building has raised different engineer’s concern since last century. The aim of this project is to develop an autonomous robot that assists the emergency evacuation of the disability and injuries in the Temporary Refuge Space and Refuge Floor. The immediate assistance is a combination of urgent medicine delivery, remotely monitor of patient’s status (from face expression judge the urgency) and task assignment from the building management office. The robot is designed to work with other smart cities system like SCADA and Building Management System (BMS) under Artificial Intelligence & Internet of Things Internet Of Thing (AIoT) network, so that the building management can access, monitor, and control the robot from anywhere in the world.
Read More »
Computer Science
Soulnos: The Lost Soul
Soulnos – The Lost Soul is a 2D single-player platform game, which player controls two characters to clear every stage. In game, player will face various challenges, including two kinds of monsters, and four kinds of traps. As the movements of the two characters are synchronised, player needs to control the characters smartly to avoid dangers in every stage. Both characters can make a melee attack to kill the monsters in the game. In addition, boosters may exist in each stage, assisting the player to clear the stage. Four kinds of booster, including jump boost, speed boost, healing boost and ranged attack boost are included. When the game is progressing, hints will be revealed to player and player will know more about the truth.
Read More »
Mechanical Engineering
HKU UAS@4th Inno Show
The team design, build, and test autonomous unmanned aerial system (UAS), which consist of a drone carrying a small unmanned ground vehicle for package delivery, to complete a mission that include autonomous flight, obstacle avoidance, object detection, mapping, and air drop. The complete system is expected to participate in unmanned aerial system related competition.
Read More »
Mechanical Engineering
Automatic Chair Stacking System
Automation is becoming much popular nowadays, ranging from household appliances to large industrial machines. The project of Automatic Chair Stacking System is aimed to showcase the idea of automatic conference room by cooperating with the Automatic Chair Parking System. The systems will be able to set up the conference room and tidy up the chairs without any manpower. The system is built with different types of mechanical drives and Arduino programming.
Read More »
Biomedical Engineering
COVID-19: Latent Clinical Phenotypes on Admission in Hong Kong across 2020
In the face of the COVID-19 pandemic, efforts in 2019 and 2020 have been devising immediate practices. However, limited knowledge on COVID-19 can lead to ineffective interventions and undesired consequences. To better understand the underlying mechanism of COVID-19, a population-based retrospective study was conducted.
It covered 7606 COVID-19 positive patients in Hong Kong across 2020. This large sample size brings great statistical power and generalizability to the results. It covers a broad disease severity spectrum and is representative of Hong Kong population.
The k-prototype clustering used here demonstrates an unprecedented strength to capture 86.6% deceased cases in one of the four clusters and identify most of the clinical characteristics of a poor prognosis without knowing them in the clustering process.
Upon further verification and investigation into these clusters, new understandings based on different clinical representations of COVID-19 will subsequently benefit disease prevention and the development of customized treatment protocols.
Read More »
First Year Engineering
Smart Soccer Robot (i) @ 4th Inno Show
Our product is a smart soccer robot that is primarily used to revolutionise the technical education industry. We designed it on SOLIDWORKS, being very careful regarding technicalities like the position of the centre of gravity and weight distribution. The materials are all environmentally friendly so that we fulfil our ethical responsibility of keeping the environment clean. The robot’s design allows it to “engulf” the ball, keeping it secure for as long as necessary. The precise mBlock programming allows it to be manoeuvred professionally. Both of these features, when coupled together, make it quite a useful product in terms of efficiency. In addition to dominating on the field, it can also serve purposes like spreading the influence of STEM education by making it more fun and stimulate students to work in teams and think critically.
Read More »
Computer Science
Roll-topia
This 3D platformer running game is about a girl falling into a dream which guides her into a world called Roll-topia. In the communication with the residents of the local villages, she learned that the villagers were frustrated with the invaders who destroyed their houses. As a result, she decided to kick up the invaders. She uses cheese to attract attention to the greedy mice on the way to protect herself. In the end, she surprisingly arrived to the beginning point, only to find out this world is in the shape of a hamster wheel.

Civil Engineering
Electrospun reusable nanofibrous membrane filters for environmental applications
Water and air pollution have become major challenges for humans in the 21 century. With limited accessible resources, a sustainable solution is needed for pollution control. Electrospun nanofibrous membranes are made of tiny fibers in nano scales with high pororsity. The special features make the membranes highly efficient and durable in pollutant adsorption. Moreover, by simple washing with easily accessible agents, the membranes can be almost fully regenerated to achieve reusability. There is high commercialization and sustainability value behind this project.

Video games, especially mobile games, can utilize AR technology to provide an immersive user experience. However, currently, most of the Mobile AR game usually lacks interactions between users and virtual objects due to the limited size and control interface of the device, nor can provide synchronized multiplayer expensive.
This project is to develop an AR interactive mobile game prototype that includes hand gesture control and world map sharing. We expect this technology can be applied in the education realm in the future.”

The robots are operated by Nvidia Jetson Nano computer, a computer specialized for AI development. The robots can reduce the long queuing time for ordering and food collection, messy dirty dishes and wastes lead to high workload on dish washing, unpopular food waste collection mechanisms and floor trash recycle in a restaurant. Therefore, the project explores the possibility of utilising the smart patrol robot for fever checking at the gate area. The project incorporated a thermographic camera on the robot and proceeded with different stages of data collection, data processing, and face recognition. A web portal has also been developed for fever case management.

moving and arranging chairs in large venues such as classrooms while
reducing the risk of occupational and ergonomic injuries. This can also

About Engineering Inno Show
Previous image
Next image
The Engineering Inno Show is a showcase carnival that celebrates innovative Engineering student projects at the end of every semester. Participating students will have the opportunity to expound on their inventive design, research and projects; harness timely and constructive feedback given by peers, teachers, industry experts and the public through knowledge exchange; and spin talent and ideas into innovative (re)inventions. There are many reasons why Engineering Inno Show is a unique concoction of its missions and vision. We offer a vibrant, inter/multi-disciplinary and hands-on learning platform for students to create their own impact, in and out of the classroom. The showcases also paint junior fellows a concrete picture of what constitutes an exemplary work and open pathways for them to look at Engineering through the lens of their senior cohorts, whether they are from Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Electrical Engineering or Environmental Engineering. We believe that Engineering united with hands-on experience is essential. It is our vision to inspire a generation of intrepid explorers and committed collaborators. At Engineering Inno Show, we are transmitting knowledge and values through narrative. Whether it is communicated in layman’s terms or field-specific terminologies, we hope that the seeds of creative minds will germinate and thrive.

Winners of Inno Show Award
We are excited to announce that the 4th Engineering Inno Show was successfully held on May 4, 2021. A total of 36 student projects from 5 departments and InnoHub members were showcased in the event. The teams have done an excellent job in preparing the event and presenting their work to classmates, teachers, and visitors. Please join us in congratulating the following five projects for receiving the Inno Show Awards:
A solar power system for producing useful fuels and chemicals from biomass waste
To design an innovative solar power system with a solar tracking system and solar power supply system, which comprises the concepts of applying solar energy and waste-to-energy, to convert biomass waste materials to char products, namely charcoal, biochar and activated carbon through pyrolysis. The solar power system is a zero-carbon emission system during operation and conversion. Furthermore, it is an economically viable system with a short payback period of less than 7 years with a minimal land requirement. It is hoped that the project will contribute to both environment and lead to the optimization of power storage to discover cost-effective designs in the future.
Introducing SURGIVIEW: A Fast and Accurate Augmented Reality(AR) Application Supporting End-to-End Clinical Operations
SURGIVIEW is a holographic augmented reality (AR) application that can assist end-to-end surgical support for minimally invasive surgeries (MIS). This app can overlay holographic anatomic structure on physical tissue, so surgeons can see “through” patient’s body during operation. Incorporating a novel triplet-calibration algorithm, the app can achieve accurate overlay (re-projection error < 5mm) faster than most of the current strategies for less than 8 seconds.
Aiming for use among medical community including surgeons, patients and medical residents, the app has multiple functions to support from pre-operative planning, intra-operative navigation to post-operative demonstration. With SURGIVIEW, we hope to develop a more intuitive and interactive future of clinical and surgery practices.
Impact of Different Factors on Hyporheic Exchange in a Meandering Pool-riffle Stream
The hyporheic zone (HZ) is the region of saturated sediment surrounding a stream which connects surface water and groundwater flow. The overlying water with dissolved matters infiltrates into the HZ, stays there for some time and interacts with groundwater, and exfiltrates out of the HZ, resulting in hyporheic exchanges (HE).
Most of the rivers are designed with narrow bottom section and large upper section of concrete streambed which results in bad river eco-system. In recent decades, more and more stream restoration projects involve the recovery of HE, however, effective guidance in restoring HE is still missing. Therefore, this study aims to examine the effectiveness of different key factors (e.g., stream discharge, slope, sinuosity and groundwater flow) in restoring HZ in a meandering channel with floodplain using flume experiments and numerical simulations.
Design and Modification of a Rototiller for the Grass/Sedge Control
WWF-HK, the management organization of the Mai Po Nature Reserve, has to offer waterbirds a mudflat without vegetation. Currently, workers are deployed into the mudflat to remove the vegetation. However this method is inefficient and dangerous. WWF-HK wishes to develop a product to reduce the necessity of sending out workers to the intertidal mudflat. Field visits were conducted to understand the design constraints. Removal methods adopted by other wetland management in the world were studied. As a result, radio-controlled hovercraft mounted with a grass cutter was chosen as the solution to the problem. The product was tested in different settings, including lawn, water and Mai Po. Results proved the product met the target specification. The product would serve as a reference for WWF-HK in future projects in vegetation removal.
ProperT
“The rights of many tenants in Hong Kong are left unenforced. Not only are the relevant regulations and clauses inaccessible and convoluted, it is also hard for the average tenant to know whom to approach when there is a “health and safety” issue in their buildings.
We develop a technology solution that would inform tenants about their rights using computer vision technology. Tenants can simply use their mobile phones to scan items in the common areas of their buildings to learn about the regulations and clauses relevant to those items. This would enable them to anonymously report these breaches for enforcement.”

BREED HKU: Robotic Fish@4th Inno Show
The robotic fish project provides aspiring engineers with a platform to gain hands-on experience in applied engineering. With design innovation, we enhance the functionality of the fish to further improve manoeuvrability and control.
Our initial goal to make the robot faster and break the world record again has been achieved. Now, the second goal is to solve real-world problems. From discussions with stakeholders, we have identified an opportunity to apply our robot in data collection for marine exploration and pollution monitoring. It can be used to collect water data such as temperature, pH, etc. and also for real-time mapping and monitoring of specimens in the environment such as coral reefs, microplastics, etc.
We envision a series of such projects under the BREED umbrella to promote bio-robotics with a purpose. Ultimately, we hope to create an organisation that drives social impact through innovative robotics solutions.

The immediate assistance is a combination of urgent medicine delivery, remotely monitor of patient’s status (from face expression judge the urgency) and task assignment from the building management office. The materials are all environmentally friendly so that we fulfil our ethical responsibility of keeping the environment clean. This project is to develop an AR interactive mobile game prototype that includes hand gesture control and world map sharing. We expect this technology can be applied in the education realm in the future.”
Read More »
Electrical and Electronic Engineering
Augmented Reality in Teaching and Learning
A common difficulty for beginner programmers is the concept of objects and references, which is more apparent when learning Python, which hides these concepts with simple semantics. This project is a mobile application that aims to use AR visualization to teach this concept, using some data types in Python. The user is able to execute supported Python statements and view an AR animation visualizing the components involved and the underlying operation. Their behavior are shown using their AR models and animations. Sandbox mode and exercise mode are available for user to explore on their own or follow exercises that showcase the properties of the data types. With the help of this application, the user can understand the concept of object and reference more clearly.
Read More »
Electrical and Electronic Engineering
Drawing Robot and Selfie Smart Phone App
For the current drawing robot products, the users use the various apps to do the image processing and Bluetooth transmission, the operation is inconvenient and complicated. For improving user experience, there is a mobile app called “Drawing Robot Controller” is developed. Users can use the mobile app to achieve a basic moving control function and image drawing function via clicking the buttons on the app. Unlike the “Printer”, the drawing robot should be “Painter” after integrating with the mobile app. The robot can draw what the user wants in different places with different styles via this app.
Read More »
Faculty of Social Sciences
Delivery of medical equipment with drones
Our project seeks to alleviate some of the health threats in Southeast Asia due to limited access to roads and healthcare facilities. It suggests the use of drones to deliver medical supplies. The design of our drone service differs from existing companies because it proposes larger service areas, incoporates the idea of a telemedicine service to reduce the need to travel for medical consultation, focuses on a supplier-to-patient network structure rather than a supplier-to-hospital network structure, and suggests using public health centers and small clinics as delivery centers if patients do not have access to phones or the internet.
Read More »
Industrial and Manufacturing Systems Engineering
Logistics delivery trajectories analysis by machine learning
“In traditional logistics operations, activities and their durations were not properly recorded. Thus, it is difficult to understand and model the daily operations.
In this project, with given trajectories, a methodology is proposed to infer the types of activities of the delivery workers in a journey.
The method is to analyze the trajectories which can be identified from the collections of GPS data collected by the devices the deliver worker carried when they are on duty.
We would want to know whether the delivery worker is traveling or delivering the goods given a trajectory segment.”
Read More »
Mechanical Engineering
HKU Racing @ 4th Inno Show
HKU Racing, the first motor racing team in HKU and the first team based in Hong Kong to compete in Formula Student (European series), was established by a group of engineering students in 2018. Electrification of the transportation system is a leading trend in the modern world, where building up a race car with the combination of the electric powertrain and the traditional mechanical system is an innovative activity. With the university’s support and the team’s effort, the team has achieved 3rd place overall in class 2 and 2nd place in design at the Formula Student 2019.
Read More »
Biomedical Engineering
COVID-19: Latent Clinical Phenotypes on Admission in Hong Kong across 2020
In the face of the COVID-19 pandemic, efforts in 2019 and 2020 have been devising immediate practices. However, limited knowledge on COVID-19 can lead to ineffective interventions and undesired consequences. To better understand the underlying mechanism of COVID-19, a population-based retrospective study was conducted.
It covered 7606 COVID-19 positive patients in Hong Kong across 2020. This large sample size brings great statistical power and generalizability to the results. It covers a broad disease severity spectrum and is representative of Hong Kong population.
The k-prototype clustering used here demonstrates an unprecedented strength to capture 86.6% deceased cases in one of the four clusters and identify most of the clinical characteristics of a poor prognosis without knowing them in the clustering process.
Upon further verification and investigation into these clusters, new understandings based on different clinical representations of COVID-19 will subsequently benefit disease prevention and the development of customized treatment protocols.

pages.text:
Performance of Sustainable Cement for Marine Construction
Course project, CIVL4102 Final year project (Coordinator: Dr. Sergio Lourenco)
Project supervisor: Dr. Hailong Ye (Department of Civil Engineering)
Project information
Project descriptions
Chloride attack of concrete in particular for marine structures is a serious global issue where it can lead to severe deterioration of the concrete, drastic reduction in strength of structures and safety concerns. The world is urging for a remedy to this situation. A green alternative to Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC), Alkaline-activated Slag (AAS), is found to be having 70%-150% higher chloride binding capacity than that of OPC, making it a potential antidote to this issue. This project aimed to analyse the chloride resistance of AAS in the marine environment, to provide better predict the service life of marine structures and to find ways to enhance the durability of concrete in aggressive conditions. With AAS, let us ‘cement’ a sustainable future.

pages.text:
Impact of Different Factors on Hyporheic Exchange in a Meandering Pool-riffle Stream
CIVL4102 Final year project
Project supervisor: Dr. T. F. May Chui (Department of Civil Engineering)
Project information
Project descriptions
The hyporheic zone (HZ) is the region of saturated sediment surrounding a stream which connects surface water and groundwater flow. The overlying water with dissolved matters infiltrates into the HZ, stays there for some time and interacts with groundwater, and exfiltrates out of the HZ, resulting in hyporheic exchanges (HE).
Most of the rivers are designed with narrow bottom section and large upper section of concrete streambed which results in bad river eco-system. In recent decades, more and more stream restoration projects involve the recovery of HE, however, effective guidance in restoring HE is still missing. Therefore, this study aims to examine the effectiveness of different key factors (e.g., stream discharge, slope, sinuosity and groundwater flow) in restoring HZ in a meandering channel with floodplain using flume experiments and numerical simulations.

Press release
HKU Engineering VAYU Project sets new Guinness World Record for “The Fastest 50m Swim by a Robotic Fish”
This article appeared in the
HKU press release
The VAYU Project set the new Guinness world record for “The Fastest 50m Swim by a Robotic Fish” on January 23, 2020, in Shenzhen.
The team had worked on the project for four years.
Previous image
Next image
Supported by the Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing(Inno Wing), a VAYU robotic fish project developed by a student team from the Faculty of Engineering at the University of Hong Kong (HKU) set the Guinness World Record of 26.79s for “The Fastest 50m Swim by a Robotic Fish” on January 23, 2020. Compared with the world records set by human swimmers in long course swimming pools ratified by International Swimming Federation (FINA), the robotic fish swim faster than women in breaststroke (29.40s
1
) and backstroke (26.98s
2
).
Robotic technology provides us with the power to explore the unknown and save human beings from life-risking tasks. However, current technology is still far from being able to recreate a robotic fish with high swimming speeds of natural fishes in open water, which has gone through millions of years of natural evolution. Although scientists have created fast-swimming fishlike-robots under steady laboratory environments, it forgoes the challenge of an open sea, where firstly, it needs to be self-contained to complete a long distance swim and secondly, to deal with the complex dynamics of the ocean.
Led by the Department of Mechanical Engineering, the VAYU Project is a joint effort with the Department of Electrical & Electronic Engineering and Computer Science of the Faculty of Engineering. More than 40 students contributed to the project over the years, and the fish development theme has made its way into several final year projects and student research projects, including a sponsored BREED project under the Inno Wing. “This project attempts to push the boundary of our understanding of robotic fishes in the real world, mimicking the behavior of real biological fishes for oceanic exploration, and as a platform for further research on natural aquatic species behaviors,” said Dr Wang Zheng, supervisor of the project.
The Project was first initiated by a BEng(CE) student, now a graduate, Sidhant Gupta. He wanted to develop a fast swimming, self-contained robotic fish which is capable of traversing long distances. He was aiming to have the fish complete a 50m swim in a long course pool within 30 seconds, while having a biomimetic propulsion specifically an undulating caudal fin. He then established a team with Shen Zhong, a PhD student of Mechanical Engineering. At the end of 2017, Mr. Timothy Ng, a recent graduate from BEng(ME), took over the role as the project lead and brought the fish to its current record breaking performance. “We had worked on this project for four years. Throughout the years, with the team constantly evolving and growing, several prototypes have been developed and a few attempts have been made to reach the 30s target,” said Timothy. “The biggest challenge is how to start building a record-breaking fish. We chose to copy the natural movements of a fish which is something robots have tried to avoid in the past, but we felt it was a pathway worth exploring. After a few successful iterations on the prototypes, we had our first ever attempt in November 2017 at the HKU Stanley Ho Sports Center and achieved the closest attempt to the world record, 50m in 34s, 4 seconds short of the existing record.”
The robotic fish went through drastic changes as the team strived to find a balance between its speed, weight, durability and reliability. After several failed attempts with different prototypes like “White Fish”, “Fat Tuna Fish” and “Yellow Tail”, the team eventually managed to instill the strength of stainless steel into 3D printed plastic, a much lighter material, and developed the latest prototype “OMEGA Fish”.
The team carried out a series of tests with “OMEGA Fish” in January 2020 at the CUHK Shenzhen Natatorium in Mainland China. They successfully made a world record-breaking time of 00:26:795’ for a 50m swim on January 23. After reviewing the full set of records and evidence, the Guinness World Record Organisation officially recognised the VAYU Project with its new world record “The Fastest 50m Swim by a Robotic Fish” of 26.79s.
Professor Christopher Chao, Dean of Engineering, is proud of the team’s achievement. He said, “Breaking a world record is not an easy task. We are so excited about the breakthrough they made. It is a result of collective effort of students from different disciplines. It is also a good example of how our students apply their professional knowledge to develop solutions with real-world impact. With this record, we hope to raise public interest in ocean exploration. We also aim to make these types of robotics projects an annual challenge among our team.”
A video on the journey of the VAYU Project:
https://youtu.be/kU3yMyuUBA0
Guinness World Record:
https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/413784-fastest-50-metres-by-a-robotic-fish

pages.title: The 4th Engineering Inno Show
pages.text:
The 4th Engineering Inno Show
"All the flowers of all the tomorrows are in the seeds of today"
Date:
4th May 2021 (Tuesday)
Time:
10:00 am – 15:00 pm
(Award ceremony at 12:45pm)
Venue:
Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing
Show me the projects
Event photo gallery
Awards & Prizes
Inno Show Award:
To encourage students to develop innovative mindset in tackling engineering and social problems, and to support outstanding ideas to join international design competitions, the Dean’s Innovation and Entrepreneurship Fund will appropriate an amount of HK$100K
to support a maximum of five student teams
participated in the Inno Show to take part in international design competitions.
A Panel to be chaired by the Associate Dean (Student Development) with the Dean of Engineering as one of the key members, will select the winning teams from the Inno Show event to be held at the end of semester 2, 2020-2021, based on the design put forward by the students, and their presentation during the Inno Show.
About Engineering Inno Show
Previous image
Next image
The Engineering Inno Show is a showcase carnival that celebrates innovative Engineering student projects at the end of every semester. Participating students will have the opportunity to expound on their inventive design, research and projects; harness timely and constructive feedback given by peers, teachers, industry experts and the public through knowledge exchange; and spin talent and ideas into innovative (re)inventions. There are many reasons why Engineering Inno Show is a unique concoction of its missions and vision. We offer a vibrant, inter/multi-disciplinary and hands-on learning platform for students to create their own impact, in and out of the classroom. The showcases also paint junior fellows a concrete picture of what constitutes an exemplary work and open pathways for them to look at Engineering through the lens of their senior cohorts, whether they are from Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Electrical Engineering or Environmental Engineering. We believe that Engineering united with hands-on experience is essential. It is our vision to inspire a generation of intrepid explorers and committed collaborators. At Engineering Inno Show, we are transmitting knowledge and values through narrative. Whether it is communicated in layman’s terms or field-specific terminologies, we hope that the seeds of creative minds will germinate and thrive.

Winners of Inno Show Award
We are excited to announce that the 4th Engineering Inno Show was successfully held on May 4, 2021. A total of 36 student projects from 5 departments and InnoHub members were showcased in the event. The teams have done an excellent job in preparing the event and presenting their work to classmates, teachers, and visitors. Please join us in congratulating the following five projects for receiving the Inno Show Awards:
Introducing SURGIVIEW: A Fast and Accurate Augmented Reality(AR) Application Supporting End-to-End Clinical Operations
SURGIVIEW is a holographic augmented reality (AR) application that can assist end-to-end surgical support for minimally invasive surgeries (MIS). This app can overlay holographic anatomic structure on physical tissue, so surgeons can see “through” patient’s body during operation. Incorporating a novel triplet-calibration algorithm, the app can achieve accurate overlay (re-projection error < 5mm) faster than most of the current strategies for less than 8 seconds.
Aiming for use among medical community including surgeons, patients and medical residents, the app has multiple functions to support from pre-operative planning, intra-operative navigation to post-operative demonstration. With SURGIVIEW, we hope to develop a more intuitive and interactive future of clinical and surgery practices.
ProperT
“The rights of many tenants in Hong Kong are left unenforced. Not only are the relevant regulations and clauses inaccessible and convoluted, it is also hard for the average tenant to know whom to approach when there is a “health and safety” issue in their buildings.
We develop a technology solution that would inform tenants about their rights using computer vision technology. Tenants can simply use their mobile phones to scan items in the common areas of their buildings to learn about the regulations and clauses relevant to those items. This would enable them to anonymously report these breaches for enforcement.”
Impact of Different Factors on Hyporheic Exchange in a Meandering Pool-riffle Stream
The hyporheic zone (HZ) is the region of saturated sediment surrounding a stream which connects surface water and groundwater flow. The overlying water with dissolved matters infiltrates into the HZ, stays there for some time and interacts with groundwater, and exfiltrates out of the HZ, resulting in hyporheic exchanges (HE).
Most of the rivers are designed with narrow bottom section and large upper section of concrete streambed which results in bad river eco-system. In recent decades, more and more stream restoration projects involve the recovery of HE, however, effective guidance in restoring HE is still missing. Therefore, this study aims to examine the effectiveness of different key factors (e.g., stream discharge, slope, sinuosity and groundwater flow) in restoring HZ in a meandering channel with floodplain using flume experiments and numerical simulations.
Design and Modification of a Rototiller for the Grass/Sedge Control
WWF-HK, the management organization of the Mai Po Nature Reserve, has to offer waterbirds a mudflat without vegetation. Currently, workers are deployed into the mudflat to remove the vegetation. However this method is inefficient and dangerous. WWF-HK wishes to develop a product to reduce the necessity of sending out workers to the intertidal mudflat. Field visits were conducted to understand the design constraints. Removal methods adopted by other wetland management in the world were studied. As a result, radio-controlled hovercraft mounted with a grass cutter was chosen as the solution to the problem. The product was tested in different settings, including lawn, water and Mai Po. Results proved the product met the target specification. The product would serve as a reference for WWF-HK in future projects in vegetation removal.
A solar power system for producing useful fuels and chemicals from biomass waste
To design an innovative solar power system with a solar tracking system and solar power supply system, which comprises the concepts of applying solar energy and waste-to-energy, to convert biomass waste materials to char products, namely charcoal, biochar and activated carbon through pyrolysis. The solar power system is a zero-carbon emission system during operation and conversion. Furthermore, it is an economically viable system with a short payback period of less than 7 years with a minimal land requirement. It is hoped that the project will contribute to both environment and lead to the optimization of power storage to discover cost-effective designs in the future.
Projects in the show
Electrical and Electronic Engineering
Drones for the purpose of Long Distance Wireless Communication based on LoRa
The main purpose of this project is to develop a cost-effective surveillance and rescue drone with a longer flying time and long-range data transmission through a careful selection of industrial quality low-cost components. Our target customers are disaster relief teams which can use the drone for assistance in rescue operations through surveillance and human detection.
The drone has the following functionality:
i) Human Detection Capabilities through PIR Sensing
ii) LoRa communication channel for transmitting human detection signals back to rescue teams
iii) Auto-Level Feature to ensure stability in turbulent weather conditions
A first prototype has been developed with all the necessary functionality and is 40% cheaper than available solutions.
Our goals for the next prototype are: i) Reduce weight to improve performance ii) Design a custom PCB to make design more compact.
Read More »
Computer Science
Automatic cars
This project is participating the Robomaster ICRA AI challenge which aims to create an automatic small car which can conduct automatic navigation, decision making, auto-aiming (for shooting other robots). During the competition, robots will automatically navigate in an 8m * 4m competition region with barriers, localize itself, find the enemy robot, aim at its armor, and shoot it!
Read More »
Electrical and Electronic Engineering
Game app for pick and place 3D printed robotic arm
This project proposed to build up a “Compact AlphaGo”. For the software part, an Android chess game application was developed by Flutter with a Flask image processing server which was developed by Python. The Minimax Algorithm and Alpha-Beta Pruning constructed a “brain” to the AI which is embedded inside the Android app. A robotic arm with a chess stacker was built by the 3D modeling software AutoCAD, the cheeses were grasped by the robotic arm precisely and placed on the correct grid of the chessboard.
Read More »
Computer Science
Supermarket Jump!
Supermarket Jump is a minigame where player can take part in a casual parkour experience. The player will play as a box of milk who does not want to be purchased and tried to jump against the conveyer belt to avoid being bought. The main objective of the game is to stay on the conveyer belt as long as possible. The player will encounter various obstacles in the process and some obstacles are deadly – touching them will immediately lead to the end of the game. Bonus points will also be offered if the player successfully performs a “risky jump”.
Read More »
Industrial and Manufacturing Systems Engineering
Logistics delivery trajectories analysis by machine learning
“In traditional logistics operations, activities and their durations were not properly recorded. Thus, it is difficult to understand and model the daily operations.
In this project, with given trajectories, a methodology is proposed to infer the types of activities of the delivery workers in a journey.
The method is to analyze the trajectories which can be identified from the collections of GPS data collected by the devices the deliver worker carried when they are on duty.
We would want to know whether the delivery worker is traveling or delivering the goods given a trajectory segment.”
Read More »
Electrical and Electronic Engineering
Drawing Robot and Selfie Smart Phone App
For the current drawing robot products, the users use the various apps to do the image processing and Bluetooth transmission, the operation is inconvenient and complicated. For improving user experience, there is a mobile app called “Drawing Robot Controller” is developed. Users can use the mobile app to achieve a basic moving control function and image drawing function via clicking the buttons on the app. Unlike the “Printer”, the drawing robot should be “Painter” after integrating with the mobile app. The robot can draw what the user wants in different places with different styles via this app.
Read More »
First Year Engineering
Dance with idols
Dance with idols is a music game. With only one smart phone or PC with one webcam, you can follow the tutorial and dance with virtual idols. The camera captures your gesture and the computer calculates the similarity between you and the model precisely. At the end of each song, you will see your final total score and grade. It lowers the requirement of devices but improves the dancing experience along with virtual idols.
Read More »
Electrical and Electronic Engineering
Augmented Reality in Teaching and Learning
A common difficulty for beginner programmers is the concept of objects and references, which is more apparent when learning Python, which hides these concepts with simple semantics. This project is a mobile application that aims to use AR visualization to teach this concept, using some data types in Python. The user is able to execute supported Python statements and view an AR animation visualizing the components involved and the underlying operation. Their behavior are shown using their AR models and animations. Sandbox mode and exercise mode are available for user to explore on their own or follow exercises that showcase the properties of the data types. With the help of this application, the user can understand the concept of object and reference more clearly.
Read More »
Computer Science
A Big Data Driven Approach for MTR and Corona Virus Analysis
This is a Big-Data project catering to the needs of researchers at The University of Hong Kong. This project’s implementation in the form of a web-based system that enables easy flow of data-retrieval, visualization, and analysis that would fuel research into the fields of COVID-19 spread and MTR passenger behavior.
Read More »
First Year Engineering
Smart Soccer Robot (ii) @ 4th Inno Show
This is a remote-controlled robot designed to play soccer matches against other robots. It is a product aimed at teenagers learning STEM education. Our design is inspired by the shape of a charging bull, which makes it more attractive to our target audience. The robot is made from mBot parts, laser-cut wooden panels, and 3D printed wheels. It is assembled using only a few screws due to our use of interlocking mechanisms integrated into the panels. The robot includes an optical sensor, and displays the number of times it crosses a black line on the seven segment display on the back.

BREED HKU: Robotic Fish@4th Inno Show
The robotic fish project provides aspiring engineers with a platform to gain hands-on experience in applied engineering. With design innovation, we enhance the functionality of the fish to further improve manoeuvrability and control.
Our initial goal to make the robot faster and break the world record again has been achieved. Now, the second goal is to solve real-world problems. From discussions with stakeholders, we have identified an opportunity to apply our robot in data collection for marine exploration and pollution monitoring. It can be used to collect water data such as temperature, pH, etc. and also for real-time mapping and monitoring of specimens in the environment such as coral reefs, microplastics, etc.
We envision a series of such projects under the BREED umbrella to promote bio-robotics with a purpose. Ultimately, we hope to create an organisation that drives social impact through innovative robotics solutions.

Fire Evacuation Assistance Robot
How occupants can evacuate during emergency in High-Rise building has raised different engineer’s concern since last century. The aim of this project is to develop an autonomous robot that assists the emergency evacuation of the disability and injuries in the Temporary Refuge Space and Refuge Floor. The immediate assistance is a combination of urgent medicine delivery, remotely monitor of patient’s status (from face expression judge the urgency) and task assignment from the building management office. The robot is designed to work with other smart cities system like SCADA and Building Management System (BMS) under Artificial Intelligence & Internet of Things Internet Of Thing (AIoT) network, so that the building management can access, monitor, and control the robot from anywhere in the world.

Computer Science
Soulnos: The Lost Soul
Soulnos – The Lost Soul is a 2D single-player platform game, which player controls two characters to clear every stage. In game, player will face various challenges, including two kinds of monsters, and four kinds of traps. As the movements of the two characters are synchronised, player needs to control the characters smartly to avoid dangers in every stage. Both characters can make a melee attack to kill the monsters in the game. In addition, boosters may exist in each stage, assisting the player to clear the stage. Four kinds of booster, including jump boost, speed boost, healing boost and ranged attack boost are included. When the game is progressing, hints will be revealed to player and player will know more about the truth.

Automatic Chair Stacking System
Automation is becoming much popular nowadays, ranging from household appliances to large industrial machines. The project of Automatic Chair Stacking System is aimed to showcase the idea of automatic conference room by cooperating with the Automatic Chair Parking System. The systems will be able to set up the conference room and tidy up the chairs without any manpower. The system is built with different types of mechanical drives and Arduino programming.
